charts.title: The design: rank pairs of concepts that are not yet linked, then count how many link later.
charts.takeaway: On the research notes the shared-neighbour ranking put 0.127 of its top 200 on pairs that linked later. Popularity alone put 0.268, and graphs rewired to keep only popularity reached a 95th percentile of 0.164.
charts.n: 3 corpora, 3 folds each; every value is the mean over the folds; 20 draws per control on the research notes

steps.label: Three dated corpora
steps.detail: Our research notes and the questions of two Stack Exchange sites, each cut into time slices. A link is two concepts in one document.

steps.label: Train on early slices
steps.detail: 3 folds. Each builds the concept graph from its training slices and scores every unlinked pair.

steps.label: Three rankers
steps.detail: Shared neighbours scores a pair by the specific neighbours its two concepts share. Popularity multiplies their link counts. Adamic-Adar was added after preregistration.

steps.label: Score on the next slice
steps.detail: A target is an unlinked pair that appears together in at least two documents of the next slice. The measure is precision in the top 200.

steps.label: Rewired and permuted graphs
steps.detail: 20 draws each on the research notes. Rewiring keeps every concept's popularity and breaks its neighbourhood. Permuting the labels breaks everything.

steps.label: Beats popularity
steps.detail: Difference interval on the research notes −0.182 to −0.125, all below 0.

steps.label: Beats both controls
steps.detail: 0.127 is below the rewired 95th percentile of 0.164. It is above the permuted one, 0.048.

steps.label: Signal with popularity held fixed
steps.detail: Area under the curve 0.569 among pairs of similar popularity, limit 0.55.

charts.title: Precision in the top 200 for each ranker on each corpus.
charts.takeaway: Popularity found more later links than shared neighbours on every corpus: 0.268 against 0.127 on the research notes, 0.088 against 0.018 on Biology and 0.043 against 0.007 on Skeptics. Adamic-Adar scored 0.273, 0.122 and 0.055.
charts.units: precision in the top 200: the share of a ranker's 200 highest-scored unlinked pairs that became linked in the next time slice.
charts.n: 3 corpora, 3 folds each; every value is the mean over the folds
charts.no_interval: The run stores an interval for the difference between shared neighbours and popularity, drawn in the next figure, and none for a single ranker or for Adamic-Adar.
charts.baseline: Base rate, the share of all unlinked pairs that are targets: 0.032 on the research notes, 0.0038 on Biology, 0.0026 on Skeptics.
charts.threshold: Shared neighbours beats popularity when the interval for the difference lies above 0. It lay below 0 on all three corpora. Adamic-Adar was not preregistered, so its lead is a pointer for a later test.

charts.title: Shared neighbours minus popularity, with its interval, on each corpus.
charts.takeaway: The difference in precision is below 0 on every corpus and no interval reaches 0: −0.142 (−0.182 to −0.125) on the research notes, −0.070 (−0.105 to −0.062) on Biology, −0.037 (−0.077 to −0.042) on Skeptics.
charts.units: difference in precision in the top 200, shared neighbours minus popularity. Below 0 means popularity found more later links.
charts.n: 3 corpora, 3 folds each; every value is the mean over the folds
charts.interval: 95% interval from resampling the test slice's documents, averaged over the folds within each draw. On Skeptics the stored difference sits just outside its stored interval; both are drawn as the run recorded them.
charts.baseline: Popularity, the product of the two concepts' link counts. A difference of 0 is a tie.
charts.threshold: Lower end of the interval above 0, on the research notes and again on Biology. Both failed: −0.182 and −0.105.

axis.label: difference in precision in the top 200

charts.title: The shared-neighbour score on the research notes against its two controls.
charts.takeaway: Graphs rewired so that each concept keeps its popularity and loses its real neighbours scored 0.146 on average, with a 95th percentile of 0.164. The real graph scored 0.127, inside and below that range. It beat only the permuted graphs, 95th percentile 0.048.
charts.units: precision in the top 200: the share of a ranker's 200 highest-scored unlinked pairs that became linked in the next time slice.
charts.n: research notes, mean of 3 folds; 20 draws per control
charts.interval: Band: 5th to 95th percentile of 20 control draws, with the control mean as a tick. The real score has no interval of its own in the run.
charts.baseline: Popularity on the real graph scored 0.268, the dashed line.
charts.threshold: Real score above the 95th percentile of both controls. It failed against rewiring, p 0.95, and held against permutation, p 0.048, the smallest value 20 draws can give.
charts.ruled_out: At the top of the list, the shared-neighbour score adds nothing detectable beyond popularity on this corpus. There was no planted check, so the study cannot say how large an effect it would have missed.

charts.title: With popularity held fixed, how well each score separates later links from the rest.
charts.takeaway: Among pairs of similar popularity the shared-neighbour score still ranks a later link above a non-link more often than a coin: 0.569 on the research notes, 0.757 on Biology and 0.696 on Skeptics. The signal is real and too weak to win the top of the list.
charts.units: area under the ROC curve within tenths of popularity: the chance that a pair that linked later scores above a pair that did not, both drawn from the same tenth. A coin gives 0.5.
charts.n: 3 corpora, 3 folds each; every value is the mean over the folds; 40,000 sampled pairs per tenth as stated in the paper
charts.no_interval: One value per corpus, the mean of three folds. The run reports no interval on it.
series_names: popularity (held fixed here, so it has no value)
charts.threshold: Above 0.55 on the research notes. It held at 0.569.

axis.label: area under the curve within tenths of popularity
